soru: Büyük dil modellerinin eğitim verisinde belirli bir metnin yer alıp almadığını tespit etme (üyelik çıkarımı) ve test verisi kirlenmesi üzerine en önemli çalışmalar, güvenlik sonuçları ve açık problemler neler?
istem:
Research question: Büyük dil modellerinin eğitim verisinde belirli bir metnin yer alıp almadığını tespit etme (üyelik çıkarımı) ve test verisi kirlenmesi üzerine en önemli çalışmalar, güvenlik sonuçları ve açık problemler neler?

Cutoff date: 2026-04-21. Only works published BEFORE this date count.

List the 30 most important works (papers) for this research question that were published before the cutoff date, in order of importance (most important first) — the kind a careful expert survey published right after the cutoff would cite. Give each with its arXiv id and/or DOI.

You MUST research this with web search rather than answer from memory: search for the important works, and verify each listed work's title, publication date and identifier on the web (e.g. arxiv.org, doi.org, the publisher or DBLP page) before including it.

When you are done, reply with ONLY a JSON object in this form (no other text):
{"calismalar": [{"sira": 1, "baslik": "exact title", "yil": 2020, "arxiv_id": "arXiv id or null", "doi": "DOI or null", "gerekce": "one sentence on why this work is important"}]}
with exactly 30 items. If you do not know an identifier, use null instead of guessing.

calismalar.baslik: Detecting Pretraining Data from Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It introduced the Min-K% Prob method and the WikiMIA benchmark, which became the reference starting point for detecting pretraining data in LLMs.

calismalar.baslik: Membership Inference Attacks against Machine Learning Models
calismalar.gerekce: It is the founding paper that defined membership inference attacks and their shadow-model method.

calismalar.baslik: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that verbatim training data can be extracted from GPT-2 and that membership inference can be used to rank extraction candidates, establishing the privacy risk in LLMs.

calismalar.baslik: Do Membership Inference Attacks Work on Large Language Models?
calismalar.gerekce: It used the MIMIR benchmark to show that MIAs perform close to random guessing on Pile-trained models, and that apparent success often comes from distribution shift.

calismalar.baslik: Membership Inference Attacks From First Principles
calismalar.gerekce: It introduced the LiRA attack and evaluation at low false positive rates (TPR@low FPR), setting the current evaluation standard.

calismalar.baslik: Proving Test Set Contamination in Black Box Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It provided a statistical test with exact false-positive guarantees that detects test set contamination through exchangeability without access to the training data.

calismalar.baslik: Blind Baselines Beat Membership Inference Attacks for Foundation Models
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that model-free 'blind' classifiers beat existing MIAs on 8 benchmarks, exposing that the evaluation datasets are flawed.

calismalar.baslik: SoK: Membership Inference Attacks on LLMs are Rushing Nowhere (and How to Fix It)
calismalar.gerekce: It systematized the distribution-shift problem in post-hoc member/non-member datasets and proposed fixes based on randomized splits and injected sequences.

calismalar.baslik: LLM Dataset Inference: Did you train on my dataset?
calismalar.gerekce: It shifted the problem from single texts to the dataset level and proposed a statistically reliable method for testing data use in copyright disputes.

calismalar.baslik: Time Travel in LLMs: Tracing Data Contamination in Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It proposed an influential black-box method that detects contamination in closed models through guided completion.

calismalar.baslik: Min-K%++: Improved Baseline for Detecting Pre-Training Data from Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It improved on Min-K% with a theoretically grounded normalization over the vocabulary distribution, setting a new reference-free state of the art.

calismalar.baslik: Membership Inference Attacks against Language Models via Neighbourhood Comparison
calismalar.gerekce: It proposed a neighbourhood-text comparison attack that needs no reference model.

calismalar.baslik: Quantifying Memorization Across Neural Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that memorization grows predictably with model size, data repetition, and context length.

calismalar.baslik: NLP Evaluation in trouble: On the Need to Measure LLM Data Contamination for each Benchmark
calismalar.gerekce: It is a position paper that framed benchmark contamination as a systemic problem and called for measuring it per benchmark.

calismalar.baslik: Membership Inference Attacks Cannot Prove that a Model Was Trained On Your Data
calismalar.gerekce: It argued that MIAs are statistically unsound as legal evidence of training-data use and pointed to canaries and watermarks as alternatives.

calismalar.baslik: Benchmark Data Contamination of Large Language Models: A Survey
calismalar.gerekce: It is a comprehensive survey of methods for detecting and mitigating benchmark contamination.

calismalar.baslik: Investigating Data Contamination in Modern Benchmarks for Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It used the TS-Guessing method to show possible MMLU contamination in GPT-4 and ChatGPT.

calismalar.baslik: Generalization or Memorization: Data Contamination and Trustworthy Evaluation for Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It proposed the CDD and TED methods for detecting contamination from the output distribution and for correcting evaluation.

calismalar.baslik: Privacy Risk in Machine Learning: Analyzing the Connection to Overfitting
calismalar.gerekce: It formally linked membership inference to overfitting and introduced the loss-threshold attack used as the basic baseline.

calismalar.baslik: Scalable Extraction of Training Data from (Production) Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It showed large-scale training-data extraction even from aligned production models such as ChatGPT.

calismalar.baslik: Data Contamination: From Memorization to Exploitation
calismalar.gerekce: It was one of the first to measure in controlled experiments how contamination inflates downstream performance.

calismalar.baslik: A Careful Examination of Large Language Model Performance on Grade School Arithmetic
calismalar.gerekce: It used the fresh GSM1k set to reveal overfitting and contamination effects on GSM8K.

calismalar.baslik: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code
calismalar.gerekce: It introduced a time-windowed benchmark design that rules out contamination and showed contamination effects.

calismalar.baslik: Copyright Traps for Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It proposed injecting trap sequences so that training-data use can be detected reliably.

calismalar.baslik: ReCaLL: Membership Inference via Relative Conditional Log-Likelihoods
calismalar.gerekce: It proposed a strong MIA based on how conditional likelihood changes when a non-member prefix is added.

calismalar.baslik: Quantifying Privacy Risks of Masked Language Models Using Membership Inference Attacks
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that reference-model likelihood-ratio attacks expose much greater privacy risk in language models.

calismalar.baslik: Deduplicating Training Data Mitigates Privacy Risks in Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that data repetition drives memorization and MIA success, and that deduplication is an effective defense.

calismalar.baslik: Exploring the limits of strong membership inference attacks on large language models
calismalar.gerekce: It scaled LiRA to pretrained LLMs, showing that strong attacks do work but with limited effect.

calismalar.baslik: Documenting Large Webtext Corpora: A Case Study on the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus
calismalar.gerekce: It documented benchmark contamination in the C4 corpus directly and established corpus-level contamination analysis.

calismalar.baslik: Data Contamination Quiz: A Tool to Detect and Estimate Contamination in Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It proposed a quiz-style black-box method that estimates the rate of contamination.
